text: haggled for a flat of bruised peaches at the Saturday market just to have a reason to talk to someone
smelled the al pastor roasting from three blocks down International and realized they hadn't eaten all day
heard the freight trains clanking near the Port and timed their breathing to the rhythm
navigated the stroller traffic on College Avenue and silently judged the parking jobs
noticed three new pop-up restaurants on Telegraph and wondered how long any of them would last
stepped over a puddle reflecting the Tribune Tower neon and thought about taking a picture
dodged the running groups circling the lake and found a quiet bench near the pergola
walked the perimeter of the Coliseum District Development and tried to picture what it would look like in five years
watched the fog roll over the port cranes from their front window
noticed another renovated Victorian on the block and calculated what the property taxes must be
walked the Mandela Parkway median under the trees and took the long way home
heard the steady thump of a bassline from three cars down at the stoplight and nodded along
passed the community clinic line and recognized three people they went to high school with
argued about the best tamale cart on International Boulevard and refused to back down
watched the ferry cut across the bay at sunset and felt lucky to live this close to the water
navigated around a film crew blocking the sidewalk near the waterfront and rolled their eyes
waited thirty minutes for a table at a brunch spot because the out-of-town friends insisted on it
walked through the alleyways behind Telegraph to avoid the weekend crowd
